articles.title: "Your system prompt is not access control. Keep user IDs in state"
articles.excerpt: The JWT was valid. The model still picked whose orders to fetch. The usual guard is one line in the system prompt: "Only show this customer's orders." Then a user asks for customer 4822's orders, the…
articles.body: The JWT was valid. The model still picked whose orders to fetch. The usual guard is one line in the system prompt: "Only show this customer's orders." Then a user asks for customer 4822's orders, the model passes 4822 to the tool, and the tool runs. A prompt is a request, not a permission check. The fix: identity goes from the verified token into run state, and the model never fills an ID the tool trusts. Scope: how identity reaches your tools, with LangChain code. Not how to stop prompt injection. What does the leak look like? Customer 4821 logs in. Your API checks the JWT, the signed login token. Valid. Then the backend writes the agent's system prompt: You are helping customer 4821. Only show this customer's orders.

articles.body: TextInput: read-only text that can't scroll on Android Issue: On Android, a read-only multiline TextInput does not scroll. If the text is taller than the box, the rest is hidden and the user cannot drag to it. The same code scrolls fine on iOS. < TextInput multiline readOnly scrollEnabled value = { transcript } style = { { maxHeight : 150 } } /> Fix: a TextInput wrapper We wrapped TextInput in one small component. When the field is multiline and read-only, it renders a ScrollView with a Text inside, in the same box. Otherwise it renders a normal TextInput.

articles.body: When I read about AI, cloud services, and security, I use several kinds of sources. Papers explain new methods, release notes describe product changes, and engineering posts describe what people tried. I look for different things in each source. One combined list can make it hard to decide what to read more closely. I use eight information-gathering routines with scheduled actions in Gemini. For papers, I ask what is new and how it might help my development work. For cloud updates, I ask whether the change could affect my systems. I treat the schedule and the questions I want a summary to answer as separate choices. Here is how I set up those requests. These are my settings as of October 13, 2026. articles.title: I built a Chrome extension that sends one prompt to 12 AI chatbots at once (no API keys)
articles.excerpt: Every day I asked ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini the same question, because the only way to know which answer is best is to compare them. That meant copy, switch tab, paste, enter, and repeat for every fo…
articles.body: Every day I asked ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini the same question, because the only way to know which answer is best is to compare them. That meant copy, switch tab, paste, enter, and repeat for every follow-up. So I built Panelize , a free, open-source Chrome/Edge extension that puts your AI chats side by side in one window. You type once, click Send All , and every panel gets the prompt. What it supports ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Doubao, Zhipu / Z.ai, Yuanbao and Google AI Mode: 12 providers, in 22 layouts from a 1×2 quick comparison to 12 at once. How it works without API keys Each panel is the provider's real web app, loaded in an iframe with your normal logged-in session.

articles.body: One of the few things that AI models are surprisingly good at is speech-to-text. A local AI model can reliably transcribe speech, and even format it for you. You’ll find dozens of third-party apps, ranging from free to $10/month subscriptions that offer to do a version of this. But Google took this to another level by integrating a polished version of this functionality directly into Gboard, appropriately named Rambler. That is, if you own a Pixel 11 series smartphone . articles.title: Gemini Skills rollout has hit a speed bump for some users
articles.excerpt: And Google says it wants to ensure a "safe and reliable" rollout for high-stakes users.
articles.body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google is delaying the rollout of Gemini skills for Workspace users. It says the rollout is on hold to ensure “safe and reliable” access for every enterprise user. Google hasn’t specified a rollout date, but says it will share an update when it is confirmed. Last month, Google confirmed its plans to sunset Gemini’s usage-specific Gems and replace them with skills. These skills are easier to set up, access, and invoke in any conversation , and they don’t force you to use them in an isolated environment like Gems did. With its announcement, Google has already started bringing skills to Gmail users , including those on Gemini’s free tiers. For enterprise users, however, Google set a later rollout date, and it has now been pushed back.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.title: 'We basically did Top Gun in space': 'Star Trek Starfleet Academy' warps back into action in March 2027 for sophomore year in the final frontier
articles.excerpt: The sophomore season of "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy" will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.
